issues.quote:
And the regulator on the wall?

DR VAUTHIER: Stopped. I looked at it, I confess, because I could not look at him for long.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about a wall regulator or any stopped clock.
issues.misreading: A solver could treat the stopped regulator as a clock reading that fixes the time of the killing, or as a second clock to reconcile with the watch and hall clock. The sheet gives no time for it, so this is an unsupported clue.

issues.quote: Piquet is the most honest way I know of losing an hour.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no game length. It says only that play lasted until a quarter to eleven by the doctor's watch, with no start time.
issues.misreading: The phrase 'losing an hour' could be read as a hint that the piquet game lasted about an hour, which would put its start near ten to ten or so and could be used to infer when play began.

issues.quote: I could see at once that he had not suffered for long. Death would have been very quick.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no information about the victim's time of death or how long it took.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this as a timing hint about when death occurred relative to the clocks, when the sheet supports no such inference.
